experiment: Exact native IBP substitution on a frozen incomplete paper-target checkpoint
scope: Single-run candidate-selection experiment. This compares two Rust substitution strategies, not AMFlow implementations or complete numerical workflows.

input.note: The saved 78,669-rule graph predates the separate conservative pilot final 85,526-rule in-memory graph; its profile is not an equal-work timing comparison.

algebra.operations: Exact factorized rational functions through public Symbolica field arithmetic; no floating conversion. Identical frozen binary and coefficient-sum policy for both strategies.
algebra.cycle_validation: Complete reachable DAG validated before pruning and again when planning the pruned graph.
algebra.zero_rules: Only RustRed Analyzer::ProvedZero terminal-sector certificates install empty rules. Existing reduction conditions and Analyzer conditions retained in raw result metadata.

provenance.implementation: MIT Expander scaffold from target/frontier-prototype/bench.rs, forced direction only; backward progress logging every 5,000 retained nodes. No Symbolica implementation was copied.

methodology.timing: Expansion uses Rust Instant. Total wall duration uses Python monotonic clock immediately before child launch through wait4; excludes provenance hashing and compilation. UTC started_utc marks preceding metadata preparation.
methodology.load: Other paper pilots and Rust compilation were active elsewhere on the host; this is a bounded exploratory run, not a repeated isolated benchmark.

correctness.exact_cross_strategy_comparison: Unavailable: forward produced no complete output before its runtime limit. The prepared rational comparator was therefore not run.
correctness.acceptance: Not achieved by this experiment: 87 nonzero three-line output terms still need searches, and previously searched residuals are not automatically certified masters.
correctness.interpretation: Supports testing an opt-in larger backward-frontier bound. No measured speedup ratio or general performance claim is made.
